body: An external review (relayed by the operator, 2026-08-22) confirmed the design's taste and named its central gap precisely: a linear hash chain detects any partial tamper, but the writer — who holds the disk, the repo, and the CI — can re-chain a forged history or truncate the tail and verify clean. The reviewer also caught four mechanical defects, all real: the gate accepted backdated-but-post-founding timestamps (monotonicity lived only in verify), anchors were unlinted decoration, the sequence regex silently dropped entry one million, and corrected entries kept their confident wording with nothing warning a reader. All four are fixed as of the commit carrying this entry; the README now states the honest threat model, and 'varve verify --expect-head' plus 'varve head' turn witnessing from aspiration into a usable mechanism. The deep fix — signed chain-head checkpoints anchored outside the writer's control — is roadmapped, not shipped. Lesson worth keeping: the constitution's sharpest sentence ('the writer, the editor, and the motivated reviser are the same party') described a threat the v1 mechanics only half-covered, and it took an outside reader one pass to see it. Being reviewed is a form of witnessing too.
title: first adversarial review: the chain cannot defend against its own writer
